scene_meta.title: Arrival in Fire
scene_meta.chronology qualification: M7 D32 is only the last-supported external-world editorial anchor inherited from Chapter 050. Chapter 051 supplies no usable elapsed external-time bridge, source-exact date, or ordinary day transition. The emergency Void Jump, crystal-acquisition travel, battlefield duration, Shadow Weaver paths, caldera descent, and Worm operation do not establish calendar advancement.
scene_meta.location: Pyroclast burning sky, aerial battlefield, and Arcturian ward
scene_meta.participants: Geralt; Oreck; coherent Luminaire; active unauthenticated Applicator; Red and Green Five Mika voices; Aelxion; surrounding Pyroclast combatants
scene_meta.focus: Survive the violent mid-air arrival, arrest the fall, secure Aelxion's cooperation, land behind the ward, and pass the brief battlefield obstacle on the way to the failing Spire.
scene_meta.boundary evidence: The emergency jump, airborne interception, controlled descent, landing, and ward fight are one continuous arrival operation. There is no time or POV reset, and the objective remains reaching and helping the Spire. Entry into the Spire begins the next scene.
scene_meta.continuity: Chapter 051 begins with an emergency Void Jump despite Chapter 050 ending with dimensional transit unavailable and a stated plan to walk. No intervening restoration or alternate jump mechanism is staged. The opening jump is agentless and must not be attributed to Luminaire.
scene_meta.presentation: Violent dimensional arrival, sustained flight, aerial interception, and brief battlefield alliance
scene_meta.cutscene purpose: Establish Pyroclast, preserve the transit contradiction, and move Geralt and Oreck to the Spire without creating a separate ward-fight scene.
scene_meta.hidden/unshown intervals: Umbra exit, promised walking, transit restoration, jump source, elapsed external time, treatment of Chapter 050 injuries, and the means by which armorless Oreck is secured during flight are absent.
scene_meta.contradictions: Sustained flight continues without repair of the bent left wing, structural compromise, or spiderweb cracking. Oreck remains armorless despite approximately 127°C ambient temperature, extreme toxicity, and an approximately seventeen-minute unprotected-survival estimate. His survival requires an unstated tolerance or protection mechanism; biology or chroniton augmentation is possible but unsourced.

scene_meta.state ledger.Dragon Mail: Stage 1 remains highest named stage; prior wing and structural damage remain unrepaired; armor absorbs additional heat and fire.

scene_meta.title: Stabilization and Departure
scene_meta.chronology qualification: M7 D32 is only the last-supported external-world editorial anchor inherited from Chapter 050. Chapter 051 supplies no usable elapsed external-time bridge, source-exact date, or ordinary day transition. The ordered operation does not permit manufactured calendar advancement.
scene_meta.location: Aetheric Coil's chamber and Luminaire's departure gate
scene_meta.participants: Geralt; Oreck; Kyh; Aetheric Coil; coherent Luminaire; Aelxion
scene_meta.focus: Confirm limited Pyroclast stabilization, preserve the continuing war, secure Kyh's campaign commitment, state the five-target arithmetic, and depart through Luminaire's gate.
scene_meta.boundary evidence: Return to Coil resets combat into aftermath, assessment, recruitment confirmation, and departure; all occur continuously in the same chamber and remain one scene.
scene_meta.continuity: Stabilized means the Worm is destroyed, the primary blockage removed, geothermal flow restored, pressure differentials stabilizing, Coil recalibrating, and the Spire returning to managed dormancy. It does not mean the war ended, Anunnaki were removed, the planet was permanently secured, crystal costs were resolved, or regional peace was achieved. Pyroclast has received time, not peace.
scene_meta.presentation: Aftermath, limited victory assessment, campaign recruitment, arithmetic, and departure
scene_meta.cutscene purpose: Close Pyroclast as the second stabilized intervention target and hand off to the next operation without overstating planetary resolution.
scene_meta.hidden/unshown intervals: Injury treatment, Hydros/Terros disposition, gate destination, and external elapsed time remain absent.
scene_meta.contradictions: Two spires stabilized and three to go confirms five total, contradicting Chapter 050's Five more to go after Umbra. The fifth target remains unidentified, and Umbrageous remains omitted from the spoken order. Chapter 052's Ghost-Spire-energy description creates a downstream gate-provenance/terminology discrepancy and does not rewrite this gate's source.
